For this, the project extends Mathlib's regularity theory, which only treats triangles, with (3) the clique counting lemma in ε-uniform parts, (4) the clique removal lemma (fewer than δn^r copies of K_r can be destroyed by deleting fewer than εn² edges) and (5) the embedding lemma for any fixed graph with a proper colouring into pairwise uniform dense parts. Mathlib has Turán's theorem, Szemerédi's regularity lemma and triangle counting/removal, but none of (1)–(5).

records.title: A converse to the discrete four-vertex theorem
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the paper "A converse to the discrete four-vertex theorem", answering Tabachnikov's Problem 2. For every n >= 4, every cyclic sequence of positive numbers with two distinct plateau maxima and two distinct plateau minima is the sequence of circumradii of consecutive vertex triples of a simple, strictly convex, coherent polygon (circumcenters inside the vertex angles). Together with Dahlberg's discrete four-vertex theorem, also proved here, this characterizes the nonconstant radius sequences of such polygons. The realization can be chosen C^1 in the data near every nonconstant admissible sequence, but an explicit path of hexagon data admits no continuous choice of realizing polygons. The analogous characterization for circles tangent to three consecutive supporting lines (the converse to Wegner's four-edge theorem) is also proved.

records.title: Erdos 662: corrected global threshold conjecture
records.abstract: Disproves an explicitly corrected global threshold formulation of Erdos problem 662. For each radius, the conjecture bounds the average number of nearby points in every sufficiently large one-separated planar set by the unit triangular lattice's neighbor count. An exact rational oblique lattice and separated finite replicas violate the bound at radius six.

records.title: Sneider's Gδ-diagonal metrization theorem
records.abstract: A compact Hausdorff space is metrizable if and only if its diagonal is a Gδ subset of its square with the product topology. The proof supplies a cofinal countable family of finite intersections of closed diagonal neighborhoods and an actual metric inducing exactly the given topology. The underlying type is arbitrary and may be empty. A general supporting theorem proves countable neighborhood character of every closed Gδ set in a compact normal space. This is classical mathematics; no novelty or priority is claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Pseudorandom hypergraph matchings (Ehard–Glock–Joos)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main results of Ehard, Glock and Joos, "Pseudorandom hypergraph matchings" (Combin. Probab. Comput. 2020): Pippenger's theorem on almost perfect matchings in almost regular hypergraphs with small codegrees (Theorem 1.1); the existence of a matching M in any r-uniform hypergraph with Δ(H) ≤ Δ, codegrees ≤ Δ^{1−δ} and at most exp(Δ^{ε²}) edges such that ω(M) = (1 ± Δ^{−ε}) ω(E(H))/Δ simultaneously for up to exp(Δ^{ε²}) weight functions (Theorem 1.2, with ε = δ/(50r²)); the generalization to weight functions on ℓ-tuples of edges, under the same exponential cap on the number of edges and of weight functions (Theorem 1.3, the main theorem, with ε = δ/(50L²r²)); the concentration inequality for pattern weights under a uniformly random colouring (Theorem 3.1); and the existence of partial Steiner systems whose subgraph counts behave as in the random model (Theorem 4.1). The formal proof is self-contained over Mathlib: Freedman's and Bernstein's inequalities are proved inside the project, and the Molloy–Reed colouring theorem used as a black box in the paper is replaced by a self-contained nibble.

records.title: A sharp asymptotic spectral bound for forbidden subgraphs
records.abstract: For every fixed finite graph F of chromatic number r+1 at least three and every positive epsilon, there is an edge threshold M such that every finite simple F-free graph G with m at least M satisfies F2(A_G) <= 2(1-1/r)m - (2(1-1/r)-1)Delta(G) + epsilon m. F2 is the sum of the squares of the two largest positive adjacency eigenvalues with missing terms padded by zero. The graphs may be disconnected. A companion theorem establishes agreement with the two largest ordered eigenvalue squares in the same eventual range. Enough edges force an F-free graph to be noncomplete; BN nonedge interlacing gives a nonnegative second ordered eigenvalue, so its positive-two energy equals the first two ordered eigenvalue squares. The proof checks ordinary clique removal through regularity and clique counting, derives weighted deletion, reuses the proved BN rank-two Gram inequality, and supplies the spectral lift, hub separation and uniform assembly.

records.title: Low-dimensional exact counterexamples to the Recht–Ré inequality
records.abstract: Five real symmetric PSD 3×3 integer matrices and five complex Hermitian PSD 2×2 Gaussian-integer matrices each have sum 100I and exact norm-of-averaged-product ratio 10329/10000 at n=k=5. The Lean statements use Mathlib positive semidefiniteness over the real and complex fields and the Euclidean operator norm. The rational formalization of De Sa's dimension-five norm-19/16 example is included as a supporting benchmark. The real symmetric dimension-two case is not resolved.

records.title: Sharp quartic Lyapunov boundaries and sextic separation for a planar cubic family
records.abstract: For a specified planar homogeneous cubic family, positive definite real homogeneous quartic Lyapunov certificates exist with strict derivative exactly when the absolute parameter is below an explicit algebraic boundary, and with weak derivative exactly through that boundary. Its value is about 2.1281535330886186. At the positive endpoint the entire cone of quartics with nonpositive derivative is one explicit nonnegative ray, without any positivity assumption. The negative Lie derivative of the endpoint quartic is a cubic square with three distinct real zero lines. Exact integer certificates separate degrees two and four at parameter two, and degrees four and six at nine fourths. The formal statements use actual partial derivatives and allow unrestricted real coefficients.

records.title: The Nash-Williams–Tutte tree packing theorem and Nash-Williams' arboricity theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three classical results on edge-disjoint trees and forests in finite simple graphs, none of which is in Mathlib. (1) The Nash-Williams–Tutte tree packing theorem: a graph has k edge-disjoint spanning trees if and only if every partition of its vertices into m parts has at least k(m − 1) edges between different parts. (2) Nash-Williams' arboricity theorem: the edges can be covered by k forests if and only if every nonempty vertex set S spans at most k(|S| − 1) edges. (3) The corollary that every 2k-edge-connected graph has k edge-disjoint spanning trees. Mathlib has no matroid union theorem and no graphic matroid; the proofs are direct edge-exchange arguments.

records.title: Erdős' theorem on graphs of large girth and large chromatic number
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Erdős' 1959 theorem: for every g and k there is a finite graph with girth greater than g and chromatic number greater than k. The formalization proves the structural form given by Erdős' probabilistic argument: for every g and every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large n there is a graph on n vertices with no cycle of length at most g in which every independent set has fewer than εn vertices; hence, for all large n, a graph on n vertices with girth greater than g that is not k-colourable. Mathlib has girth and chromatic number but not this theorem; Mycielski's construction (registered separately by another author) gives triangle-free graphs only.

records.title: Rényi and Tsallis entropy monotonicity for Bernoulli sums
records.abstract: Lean formalization of coordinatewise Rényi and Tsallis entropy monotonicity for finite independent Bernoulli sums on the closed half cube, for every real order in [0,2], as stated in Hillion-Johnson Conjecture 4.4. The complete core proves both entropy comparisons and the finite inverse-score association inequality. Concrete coefficient-law and entropy definitions are checked separately. VERIFICATION.md defines exact-source Linux acceptance and distinguishes historical association-only checkpoints.

records.title: Compact Hausdorff countable-network metrization
records.abstract: For an arbitrary compact Hausdorff space, metrizability and second countability are each equivalent to the existence of a countable network of arbitrary subsets. A genuine Urysohn-function construction from pairs of network elements supplies continuous separation, and a compatible metric induces exactly the original topology. Supporting results give bounded-real-coordinate closed embeddings, preservation under continuous surjections, arbitrary-subspace heredity and compact-subspace metrization. Empty spaces and arbitrary universes are allowed. This is classical mathematics; no novelty or priority is claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The connected size-Ramsey number of a four-edge matching versus a quadrilateral
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization project for the connected size-Ramsey equality rhat_c(4K2, C4) = 17. The intended proof uses a universal C4 vertex-transversal bound 4 tau_4(G) <= |E(G)|, a classification of the connected equality cases through sixteen edges (C4, the 4-wheel, K_{3,3} minus an edge, the octahedron), an avoiding-colouring construction from a three-vertex transversal, and an explicit twelve-vertex, seventeen-edge host. Proofs are complete as of commit c8d54e2 (2026-10-17); the proof certificate is Solution.lean and its dependency closure. Formal adversary pass 1 and reviewer pass 1 are ACCEPT_WITH_FIXES (fixes applied); the CI comparator passed at 38bd345 (2026-10-17) with five records. A sixth record, the transversal half of Corollary C (SizeRamsey.connected_transversal_le_three), was registered on 2026-10-17 (commit cc2aec2); the CI comparator passed with six records at 46bf2d0 (2026-10-17, run 39034260971).

records.title: Growth series of the triangle Coxeter groups (p, q, infinity), with the PGL(2,Z) instance: Padovan sphere sizes and growth rate the plastic number
records.abstract: Kernel-checked proof, for every Coxeter system on three generators a, b, c with m(a,c) = p, m(b,c) = q, m(a,b) = infinity and p, q >= 2, of the growth-series identity in the ring of integer power series: (sum_n a(n) X^n) * (1 - (X + ... + X^(p-1))(X + ... + X^(q-1))) = (1 + X)(1 + ... + X^(p-1))(1 + ... + X^(q-1)), where a(n) is the number of group elements of Coxeter length n; together with its instances (2,3,inf), (2,4,inf), (3,3,inf) and, for (2,3,inf) = PGL(2,Z), the sphere sizes 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 12, 16, ..., the Padovan identity a(n) = Pad(n+5) for n >= 2, the two-sided bounds 2 rho^n <= a(n) <= 4 rho^n (n >= 2), and the growth rate a(n)^(1/n) -> rho, the plastic number, the unique real root > 1 of x^3 = x + 1; and, for the whole family, monotonicity and symmetry in (p, q), the growth rate of every hyperbolic member, and the minimality of the plastic number. Twenty compared theorems: (1) the general identity for all p, q >= 2; (2) non-vacuity, a Coxeter matrix of that type exists for all p, q >= 2; (3)-(5) the three instances; (6) the (2,3,inf) sphere sizes a(0..4) = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and the recursion a(n+5) = a(n+3) + a(n+2) for all n; (7) that the recursion fails one step earlier, a(4) != a(2) + a(1); (8) a(n) = Pad(n+5) for n >= 2, for any sequence with the Padovan initial values and recursion; (9) existence and uniqueness of the plastic number; (10) the bounds; (11) the n-th-root limit; (12) monotonicity: a(n) of a (p,q,inf) system is at most a(n) of a (p',q',inf) system for p <= p', q <= q'; (13) symmetry in p and q; (14) 2 rho^n <= a(n), n >= 2, for every hyperbolic member; (15) for (p,q) != (2,2) exactly one tau > 1 solves (tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(p-1))(tau^-1 + ... + tau^-(q-1)) = 1; (16) a(n)^(1/n) -> tau; (17) tau strictly increasing in (p,q); (18) rho <= tau with equality exactly at (2,3), (3,2), so the plastic number is the minimal growth rate of the family; (19) tau < 2; (20) tau -> 2 as p, q -> infinity (for every sigma < 2 there is N with tau > sigma whenever p, q >= N). The family statements (12)-(20) give the growth rate of every hyperbolic (p, q, inf) group as the unique root tau > 1 of an explicit equation, strictly increasing in the labels, with the plastic number as the family minimum attained only at (2,3,inf) and (3,2,inf); they restrict to this family, and kernel-check there, Terragni's monotonicity (2016, Thm. A), Floyd's planar minimality (1992, p. 482) and the continuity of the growth rate (Floyd 1992; Yukita 2024). The mathematics is classical and no novelty is claimed for it: the growth series of a Coxeter group is rational and determined by its finite parabolic subgroups (Steinberg 1968; Humphreys 1990 Section 5.12); growth of planar hyperbolic Coxeter groups is Floyd 1992 and Cannon-Wagreich 1992, and the (2,3,inf), (2,4,inf) and (3,3,inf) sphere sequences are OEIS A096231, A179070 (shifted) and A054886, with generating functions derived there from Cannon-Wagreich Prop. 3.1 and, for A096231, the Padovan form a(n) = A000931(n+10) recorded; Floyd 1992 (p. 482) proves (2,3,inf) minimal among cusped planar groups and Kellerhals 2013 gives an alternative proof; Bucher-Talambutsa 2016 Prop. 18 proves statement (11) itself by a normal form and, with Mann's bound, the minimality of rho for PGL(2,Z) over all generating sets. The (p, q, inf) family is hyperbolic exactly when (p, q) differs from (2, 2); the affine (2, 2, inf) is included in (1). The contribution claimed is the kernel-checked general identity for all p, q at once, and the family statements (12)-(20) derived from it, from Mathlib's CoxeterSystem alone — Mathlib at this pin has no growth series, no exchange or deletion property and no parabolic-subgroup API — by constructing the amalgam normal forms, lifting their action to the group, proving Coxeter length equals normal-form length, and counting. No "first formalization" claim is made. Application, cited and not a claim of the entry: the (2,3,inf) group is the Weyl group of AE_3 = PGL(2,Z) (Feingold-Frenkel 1983) and, in the Damour-Henneaux-Nicolai billiard description of the Belinski-Khalatnikov-Lifshitz limit (a conjecture for generic singularities, Henneaux-Persson-Spindel 2008 Section 2.9), the reflection group of the billiard of 3+1-dimensional vacuum gravity near a spacelike singularity (Damour-Henneaux-Nicolai 2003 Section 8; Henneaux-Persson-Spindel 2008 Section 3.1), where a(n) counts the chambers reachable from the fundamental chamber after exactly n wall collisions over all initial data, so (10)-(11) give the growth rate of those outcomes (elementary reflection-group geometry, not formal content). Hypotheses are inline: the Coxeter system enters through Mathlib's CoxeterSystem with the three matrix entries as hypotheses, rho through its defining equation and 1 < rho, the Padovan sequence through its initial values and recursion; the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (CoxeterMatrix, CoxeterSystem, CoxeterSystem.length, Nat.card, PowerSeries.mk, Finset.range/Ico sums, Filter.Tendsto, Filter.atTop, nhds, real powers) — zero custom definitions. The pinned source of each Coxeter-specific imported definition, and of Nat.card and PowerSeries.mk, is quoted verbatim, with permalinks, in MATHLIB_DEFINITIONS.md (the remaining vocabulary is standard Mathlib and is not quoted), and DefinitionAudit.lean kernel-checks the facts the statements rely on (the entry 0 encodes infinity; length is the minimal word length; spheres are finite and Nat.card is their cardinality; every Coxeter matrix has a Coxeter system).

records.title: First Betti numbers of five-generated numerical semigroups
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization project for (F) an explicit two-parameter family of minimally five-generated numerical semigroups <m, m+1, m+k, m+2k-1, m+2k>, m = 2kq+1, whose toric ideal has spanRank exactly 4k+2. Planned scope for (W), a proposed finite-width bound beta1 <= 2w+2 (4 <= w <= 40), not all formalized: the generic fiber-graph infrastructure, both algebraic bridges (only the upper bridge is formalized; the reverse bridge is not), the corrected singleton-counting decomposition beta1 + p = 5 + N, the pair-component antichain lemma and certificate-checker soundness (not yet written). Version 1 targets F; W is stated and excluded from the release comparator. F is sorry-free at 793e759.

records.title: Countable-coordinate factorization for compact products
records.abstract: Every continuous map from an arbitrary product of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces into a metrizable space factors continuously through a countable subproduct. A uniform-space proof establishes countable coordinate dependence for uniformly continuous maps into separated countably generated uniform spaces. The factor for a fixed coordinate set is unique. Countably many maps share a countable coordinate set. Continuous injections into metrizable targets force only countably many nontrivial factors, giving the exact metrizability criterion for nonempty compact Hausdorff products. Empty index and empty selected-coordinate sets are allowed. These are classical results and no novelty or priority is claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: NumericalSemigroups: Huang's quadratic form, its positivity, and its n-generator kernel windows
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization around the quadratic form Q(n) = sum_{i,j in G} K(g(j) - g(i)) n_i n_j of Y. Huang (arXiv:2604.13238) on the gap diagram G of the numerical semigroup <a,b>, in two parts. Part A (Huang's results, two generators): the symmetric bilinear form B of Q satisfies B(1_D, 1_E) = dinv(D, E) for subdiagrams D, E (Huang's Theorem 1.2, formalized by AxiomProver and included in `Dinv/AxiomProver.lean`); from it this work proves Q(1_D) = dinv(D) and Q(1_D) > 0 for nonempty D (Theorem 1.1), B >= 0 on the cone of nonnegative decreasing functions, and the bound Q(n) >= n_i^2 / |G| for every coordinate i (Theorem 1.3, so Q(n) >= ||n||_inf^2 / |G|), which settles Huang's positive-definiteness conjecture for Q on that cone; Theorem 1.3 had not been formalized. Part B (the author's manuscript "A Linear Algorithm for Huang's Quadratic Form on Numerical Semigroups and Density Asymptotics", Flamandzki, 2026): for generators p_1,...,p_n the generalised kernel K^(n)(d) is the inclusion-exclusion sum over sub-multisets S of the generators of (-1)^|S| times the indicator of d >= sigma(S), where sigma(S) is the sum of S; it is a step function whose jumps are the parity function pi(s) = K(s) - K(s-1). Part B states and proves: (1) for two generators a < b, Q equals the sliding-window form sum_k n_k (W+_k - W-_k); (2) for any nonempty generator list, Q(n) is a sum over the breakpoints s of K of pi(s) times the tail pair-sum T(s) = sum_{j-i >= s} n_i n_j, with at most sigma + 1 breakpoints, and the number w of active windows (intervals between consecutive breakpoints on which K is nonzero) is at most sigma, and at most 2^n - 2 for n >= 2 distinct positive generators; and (3) for strictly increasing generators p_k >= 2 with log p_n = o(n), the density w(n)/(2^n - 1) is o(P(n)) where P(n) = prod (1 - 1/p_k), equivalently delta(n)/P(n) tends to 1 for delta(n) = P(n) - w(n)/(2^n - 1). The complexity claims of the manuscript (running times of the algorithms) and its computational tables and conjectures are not formalized. The substance of Part B is the exact breakpoint decomposition of Q, the identification of the inclusion-exclusion kernel with its recursive form, and the asymptotic squeeze. Zero sorries; depends only on the three standard Lean axioms. The file `Dinv/AxiomProver.lean` is third-party code under the MIT license (see NOTICE); everything else is Apache-2.0.

records.title: Optimal Local Decompression: Uniform Finite-View Reduction
records.abstract: A uniform finite-view reduction at the paper's counting-optimal k-bit vertex budget for odd maximum degree 2k-1. Given one total finite-view orientation rule with a sufficient one-bit advice guarantee, one decoder family is chosen before graph order, topology, markers, advice and payload. Every connected graph on Fin n with n>16(k+1) and degree at most 2k-1 admits an encoder recovering every edge bit at either endpoint from a 2^k-symbol vertex alphabet. The same total decoder is local across different connected graphs and arbitrary labelings, with no marker validity or encoded-input premise. Its explicit physical radius depends only on k and the oracle's radius, not n. Eight selected endpoints also cover storage capacity, advice-first coding, complete-graph counting, and bounded connected cell geometry. The external orientation algorithm, computability, general identifier assignments for the assembled theorem and mixed-component assembly remain outside the selected formal scope.

records.title: Moore graphs of diameter two: the Hoffman–Singleton theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Hoffman–Singleton theorem on Moore graphs of diameter two. For a finite k-regular graph of diameter at most two: the Moore bound n ≤ k² + 1; if moreover the girth is at least five, then n = k² + 1 and the graph is strongly regular with parameters (k² + 1, k, 0, 1); and, if k ≥ 2, then k ∈ {2, 3, 7, 57}. Mathlib has strongly regular graphs and the spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices, but not this theorem.

records.title: Countable-density Hewitt–Marczewski–Pondiczery theorem
records.abstract: A product of at most continuum many separable topological spaces is separable. The proof constructs a countable family of finite binary tables that realizes every finite assignment of natural-number labels, then applies dense sequences in the factors. No separation, metrizability, compactness or countable-base assumption on the factors is needed. Empty factors and empty index sets are allowed. A companion theorem proves the sharp criterion for discrete Boolean cubes: Bool^I is separable exactly when the index cardinality is at most continuum. This is the classical countable-density case; no arbitrary-cardinal or algebraic generalization, novelty or priority is claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Chvátal's and Pósa's degree conditions for Hamiltonian cycles
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two classical degree-sequence conditions for Hamiltonicity of a finite simple graph on n ≥ 3 vertices with degrees d₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ dₙ. Chvátal's theorem (1972): if for every i < n/2, dᵢ ≤ i implies d_{n−i} ≥ n − i, then the graph is Hamiltonian (stated without sorting: if at least i vertices have degree at most i, then at least i + 1 vertices have degree at least n − i). Pósa's theorem (1962): if for every k with 1 ≤ k < (n − 1)/2 fewer than k vertices have degree at most k, and, for odd n, at most (n − 1)/2 vertices have degree at most (n − 1)/2, then the graph is Hamiltonian. Mathlib has Hamiltonian cycles but neither theorem.

records.title: The graph removal lemma for every fixed graph
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the graph removal lemma of Erdős, Frankl and Rödl for an arbitrary fixed finite graph H on k vertices: for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0, depending only on H and ε, such that every finite graph on n vertices with fewer than δ nᵏ labelled copies of H can be made H-free by deleting fewer than ε n² edges; equivalently (far form), a graph from which at least ε n² edges must be deleted to destroy all copies of H has at least δ nᵏ labelled copies. Also included is the counting lemma used in the proof: if parts s x (one for each vertex x of H) are robustly dense with density at least d along the edges of H, with 2kη ≤ dᵏ and #(s x) ≥ 4k/dᵏ, then at least (dᵏ/4)ᵏ ∏ #(s x) injective maps send H into G with f x ∈ s x. Mathlib has the regularity lemma and the triangle removal lemma, but not the removal lemma for a general H.

records.title: Additive strengthening of Erdos problem 679: a known refutation
records.abstract: For every real additive constant C and natural cutoff K, every sufficiently large natural n admits K < k < n with omega(n-k) at least log(k)/log(log(k)) + C. Here omega counts distinct prime factors. This independently implemented proof uses a fixed primorial residue window, elementary Chebyshev estimates and Stirling bounds. It refutes the known additive strengthening and does not resolve the main multiplicative question. No mathematical novelty is claimed.

records.title: Tamper-proofing with self-modifying code: threat model, security and necessity of the assumptions
records.abstract: Formalizes Gregory Morse and Tamas Kozsik's paper "Tamper-Proofing with Self-Modifying Code" (arXiv:2604.12407v1). The selected statement (PalomarSMT.mathematical_result, four results T1-T4) is an abstract threat model for checksum units whose opcode state lives in the memory they checksum: a system of units with regions and code, a timeline of write, execute, check, split-view and DMA events, adversary levels L0-L4, a cost contract with lower bounds on emulation, forgery and mediation, and eight structural assumptions A1-A8 (none of the form "the attacker is detected"). An effective alarm needs a unit with a response code (at least one response byte, all of it unmodified) and either a value mismatch or a positive number k of consecutive timing failures; A6 therefore includes k > 0 and A7 includes that every unit has a response byte. The four selected results are: for every well-formed timeline of a system satisfying A1-A8, if a protected byte outside the SMC opcode bytes (which legitimately vary) is executed while the fetch view differs from the original image, an effective alarm occurs somewhere in the timeline, not necessarily before that execution (T1; executing a changed protected opcode byte is outside the goal); in a faithful split-view run every iteration with a non-zero toggle (apart from the last) is mediated, and under A3 and A5 a faithful mediated check that the cost contract admits, with such an iteration, is a timing failure (T2; not every split-view attack is claimed detected); each of the eleven assumptions is necessary, by an explicit winning adversary against a system that satisfies all the others (T3); and every well-formed timeline at level L0 or L1 with the inline timer satisfies A1, A4 and A5, while there are winning adversaries against systems satisfying every other assumption at L1 with an operating-system timer, at L2 and at L4 (T4: the removed assumption is A5 at L1 with an operating-system timer and at L2, A1 at L2, A4 at L4). Proved in the same development but NOT part of this record (they are not in the Comparator configuration): the paper's Harvard/von Neumann observation (C01, C02), a general fact about observation-preserving simulation whose time bound assumes the per-read charge it uses; the three-quadword forgery of the checksum and the proof that two quadwords do not suffice (the selected T3 witness for A8 is a single two-quadword collision pair); the x86-64 model of the kernels, the static kernel against its C emulation, the 296-unit unrolled kernel at an abstract level and at the instruction level, the byte layout against assembler output, a clear-count contract checked against the paper's tables, timers, the noise estimator, the detection predicate and the data ratios, and native test vectors for the corrected sources.

records.title: Tutte's f-factor theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Tutte's f-factor theorem: a finite simple graph G has a spanning subgraph H with deg_H v = f v for every vertex v if and only if, for all disjoint vertex sets S and T, q(S, T) ≤ ∑_{v ∈ S} f v − ∑_{v ∈ T} f v + ∑_{v ∈ T} deg_{G−S} v, where q(S, T) is the number of connected components C of G − (S ∪ T) for which ∑_{v ∈ C} f v + e(C, T) is odd and deg_{G−S} v is the number of neighbours of v outside S. Mathlib has Tutte's 1-factor theorem but not the f-factor theorem.

records.title: Chordal, split, threshold and cograph structure
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical structure theorems for finite simple graphs. Chordal graphs: every minimal a–b separator is a clique, a nonempty finite chordal graph has a simplicial vertex, and a connected non-complete one has two non-adjacent simplicial vertices (Dirac 1961); a finite graph is chordal iff it has a perfect elimination order (Fulkerson–Gross 1965), iff it is the intersection graph of subtrees of a finite tree (Gavril 1974); a nonempty finite chordal graph has treewidth ω − 1, and every finite graph has ω ≤ tw + 1. Split graphs: split iff the graph and its complement are chordal, iff no induced 2K₂, C₄ or C₅ (Földes–Hammer 1977). Threshold graphs: threshold iff no induced 2K₂, C₄ or P₄ (Chvátal–Hammer 1977), iff split and a cograph (no induced P₄). Mathlib has none of these graph classes; their definitions are stated in the Challenge.

records.title: Elementary bounds for Erdos problem 684
records.abstract: Let U(n,k) be the full prime-power part of the binomial coefficient n choose k supported on primes at most k. For all sufficiently large n, there exists k at most n with k at most 514(log n)^2 and U(n,k) greater than n squared. For arbitrarily large n greater than one, U(n,k) equals one throughout k at most (log n)/8. This independent Mathlib-only implementation adapts the known residue averaging and prime-power obstruction of APSSV26 with coarse Chebyshev constants. It does not formalize that paper's sharper coefficients or Bae's stronger registered lower bound. The optimal order remains open and no mathematical novelty is claimed.

records.title: Planar Pólya–Szegő Buckling Inequality
records.abstract: Lean formalization proving the planar Polya-Szego conjecture for the first buckling eigenvalue. For open planar sets of positive finite area, it proves the sharp area inequality and characterizes equality by exact equality with an open disk. It retains the original Sobolev-space, variational eigenvalue and Bessel definitions, and includes the disk eigenvalue and buckling–Dirichlet comparison.

records.title: Jaeger's 4-flow and 8-flow theorems and Seymour's 6-flow theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Jaeger's 4-flow theorem: every finite 4-edge-connected simple graph has a nowhere-zero integer 4-flow, i.e. an antisymmetric function on darts with values in {±1, ±2, ±3} that is conserved at every vertex. Also proved: a graph with two edge-disjoint spanning trees has its edges covered by two even subgraphs (a nowhere-zero ℤ₂ × ℤ₂-flow) and has a nowhere-zero integer 4-flow. Version 2 adds Jaeger's 8-flow theorem: every finite bridgeless graph has its edges covered by three even subgraphs and has a nowhere-zero integer 8-flow; conversely a graph with a nowhere-zero flow has no bridge. Version 3 adds Seymour's 6-flow theorem (every finite bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero integer 6-flow) and Tutte's theorem relating group and integer flows (for k > 0, every nowhere-zero ℤ/k-flow φ lifts to a nowhere-zero integer k-flow ψ with ψ ≡ φ mod k, and conversely an integer k-flow reduces modulo k to a nowhere-zero ℤ/k-flow). Mathlib has no flows.

records.title: Normalizers of Γ_Δ(N), Γ(N) and ±Γ₁(N)
records.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, about the normalizers in SL₂(ℝ) of the groups Γ_Δ(N) between Γ₁(N) and Γ₀(N), and the quotients Nor(Γ)/Γ, the modular automorphism groups of the curves X_Δ(N): a generalization of Newman's description of the normalizer to Γ_Δ(N); Nor(Γ(N)) = SL₂(ℤ), so the modular automorphism group of X(N) is SL₂(ℤ/N)/{±1}; and, for N ≠ 4, Nor(±Γ₁(N)) is generated by Γ₀(N) and the Atkin–Lehner elements, so X₁(N) has 2^ω(N) φ(N)/2 modular automorphisms for N ≥ 3 (N = 4 is an exception). 34 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Dirac's theorem: k vertices of a k-connected graph lie on a common cycle
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Dirac's 1960 theorem: in a k-connected finite simple graph with k ≥ 2 (more than k vertices, and connected after deleting any set of fewer than k vertices), any set of at most k vertices lies on a common cycle. In particular, in a 2-connected finite graph any two vertices lie on a common cycle. Cycles are Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Walk.IsCycle`. Mathlib does not have this theorem.

records.title: The normalizer of Γ₀(N): Newman's theorem, and the order and presentations of B(N)
records.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, about B(N) = Nor(Γ₀(N))/Γ₀(N), the normalizer of Γ₀(N) in SL₂(ℝ) modulo Γ₀(N), for every N ≥ 1: Newman's theorem describing the normalizer, in both directions; the order |B(N)| = 2^ω(n) ψ(N)/ψ(n), where h is the largest divisor of 24 with h² ∣ N and n = N/h²; generators and complete presentations of B(N) for every N; a criterion for B(N) to be the internal direct product of its local factors; B(18) ≅ S₄; and the errors in the published presentations: the Akbaş–Singerman relation fails in B(256), and Bars's presentations at levels 32, 64 and 128 define infinite groups, while completed presentations present B(32) and B(64) and Bars's presentation at level 256 presents B(256). 36 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Modular automorphisms of Cartan modular curves of prime level
records.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, about the normalizers in SL₂(ℝ) of the groups defining the split and non-split Cartan modular curves and their normalizer curves: for any level N, every element of the normalizer of a group containing Γ(N) is a rational matrix of a restricted form; X_sp(N) ≅ X₀(N²); X_sp(p) (p ≥ 5) and X_ns(p) (p odd) have exactly 2 modular automorphisms; X_sp⁺(p) (p ≥ 7) and X_ns⁺(p) (p ≥ 5) have none, and both bounds on p are sharp. 17 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Fréchet–Urysohn Σ-products of first-countable spaces
records.abstract: The countable-support Sigma-product of arbitrary first-countable topological factors, relative to an explicit basepoint and with the ordinary product-induced topology, is Frechet-Urysohn. An adaptive finite-coordinate schedule constructs a sequence from each set converging to any of its closure points. The index set may be arbitrary, including empty, and no separation assumption is used for this theorem. Companions give countable tightness and subspace inheritance, density in the full product, T1 countable-closure support control and sequential closedness, and nonsequentiality of an uncountable discrete Boolean cube. No normality, W-space, arbitrary Frechet-factor, compactness or novel-mathematics result is asserted.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: The local dynamical structure of Δ* sets via a new Furstenberg family algebra
records.abstract:
This development formalizes in Lean 4 the results of the paper "The local dynamical structure of Δ* sets via a new Furstenberg family algebra", which strengthens the connection between the combinatorics of difference sets and the dynamics of group rotations.
Let S be a discrete semigroup. A set A ⊆ S is syndetic if there is a finite F ⊆ S with S = ∪_{f ∈ F} f⁻¹A; a Δ set if there is a sequence s₁, s₂, … in S with s_j ∈ s_i A for all i < j; and a Bohr_0 set if it contains the preimage of an open neighborhood of the identity under a semigroup homomorphism from S to a finite-dimensional torus. Dually, a set is thick, a Δ* set, or a set of Bohr recurrence according as it meets every syndetic, every Δ, or every Bohr_0 subset of S. Bohr_0 sets in the integers are the almost periodic sets of classical interest, and Δ* sets are combinatorially large, being syndetic and rich in additive patterns.
The definition of a Δ set used here is the one given for general semigroups by Hindman, who calls these rQ sets, Q for quotient; in a commutative semigroup his left- and right-handed variants agree. It does not require the witnessing sequence to be injective, and so is slightly more inclusive than the classical difference-set definition. In the positive integers the two agree exactly: if A consists of positive integers and s_j − s_i ∈ A for all i < j then the sequence is strictly increasing, so A contains the difference set (S − S) ∩ ℕ of the infinite set S = {s₁, s₂, …}, and conversely. The two notions separate only in a semigroup containing an element a with sa = s for some s, where the constant sequence makes every set containing such an a a Δ set. In the integers the element 0 is of this kind, so a Δ set in the present sense is either a classical difference set or a set containing 0, and a Δ* set is exactly a classical Δ* set that contains 0.
The main result (Theorem A) is that Δ* sets in an arbitrary commutative semigroup carry local Bohr structure: if A ⊆ S is a Δ* set, then for every thick H ⊆ S there is a thick H′ ⊆ H and a Bohr_0 set B with A ∩ H′ = B ∩ H′. This generalizes results of Bergelson, Furstenberg and Weiss and of Host and Kra from the positive integers to arbitrary commutative semigroups by a purely topological-dynamical route in place of the ergodic- theoretic arguments used in the integer case. Theorem B is the dual formulation, in terms of Δ sets and sets of Bohr recurrence, that the proof actually establishes: if A ⊆ S admits a thick H such that A ∩ H′ is a set of Bohr recurrence for every thick H′ ⊆ H, then A is a Δ set. Theorem C exhibits a second instance of local structure by the same method: in a countable commutative semigroup, every C* set agrees with an IP* set on a thick subset of any prescribed thick set.  Theorem C also formulates the equivalent dual statement, just as Theorem B is in relation to Theorem A.
Theorem D supplies the algebraic framework the arguments rest on. A Furstenberg family on a set S is an upward-closed collection of subsets of S. On the Furstenberg families of a non-empty set, two binary operations, family meet and family join, are described and shown to be associative, commutative and monotone. Together with the family dual, they satisfy De Morgan-type laws. Family join has appeared before in the literature; family meet, as presented here, is believed to be new. The algebra reduces the equivalence of Theorems A and B to a short computation and makes similar reformulations in Ramsey theory routine.
The proofs of Theorems A and B depend on a companion result, formalized here but the subject of another Palomar entry, that the regionally proximal relation is an equivalence relation for minimal actions of commutative semigroups. The development runs to roughly 20,000 lines of Lean across 17 files and formalizes every lemma, proposition, corollary and theorem of the paper; the registered statements are Theorems A, B, C and D. Proved along the way, and not available in Mathlib, is the classical fact that the characters of a compact abelian group separate its points.

records.title: Spectral bounds on the chromatic and independence numbers
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical eigenvalue bounds for a finite simple graph G on a nonempty vertex type, with λ_max and λ_min the largest and smallest eigenvalues of its real adjacency matrix: the average degree is at most λ_max and λ_max is at most the maximum degree (Collatz–Sinogowitz); G is (⌊λ_max⌋ + 1)-colourable (Wilf 1967); if G has an edge, every proper colouring uses at least 1 − λ_max/λ_min colours (Hoffman 1970); and if G is k-regular with k ≥ 1, every independent set has at most n(−λ_min)/(k − λ_min) vertices (Hoffman's ratio bound). Mathlib has the spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices but none of these bounds.

records.title: Normalizers of the congruence subgroups Γ_H
records.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, about the normalizers in SL₂(ℝ) of every congruence subgroup Γ ⊇ Γ(N), that is, of every Γ_H for H ≤ SL₂(ℤ/N): Nor(Γ)/Γ is finite, of order at most [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ]·Σ_{D ∣ N} ψ(D); the local restrictions of Dose–Lido–Mercuri on the determinants of normalizing matrices; if, at every p ∣ N, H mod p fixes no line or H mod p^{v_p(N)} lies in a split Cartan subgroup, then Nor(Γ_H)/Γ_H ≅ N(H)/H; and at prime level the order is always [N(H) : H], or 2·[N(H) : H] when H fixes exactly one line. 21 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Distinct prime divisors of central binomial coefficients
records.abstract: A formal proof of the classical asymptotic omega(binomial(2n,n)) times log n divided by n tending to log 4. The proof combines prime-power estimates, central-binomial bounds, a prime-factor cutoff, and elementary logarithmic limits; it does not use the prime number theorem. This strengthens the earlier finite lower-bound package to a full asymptotic theorem. It does not solve the uniform conjecture in Erdos problem 685 and claims no new mathematical theorem.

records.title: The Arithmetic of Time: the slowest settling clock on at most three letters is the Padovan substitution, unique up to mirror image, and both minimal rules are chiral
records.abstract: Five compared theorems. Among all substitutions on at most three letters whose incidence matrix has a Pisot eigenvalue θ > 1, the least such θ is the plastic number ρ, the real root of x³ = x + 1, attained only by the Padovan rule a ↦ b, b ↦ c, c ↦ ab and its mirror c ↦ ba, up to renaming the letters; both minimal rules are chiral, in opposite directions. Precisely: (1) for a substitution σ on k ≤ 3 letters (images may be empty) and a real eigenvalue θ > 1 of its integer incidence matrix that is a Pisot number, ρ ≤ θ, and θ = ρ exactly when, after renaming the letters, σ is the Padovan rule or its mirror; no primitivity or unit hypothesis; (2) the same classification for every real eigenvalue, with no Pisot hypothesis; (3) a 3 × 3 natural matrix with characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1 is the Padovan matrix after one simultaneous permutation of rows and columns; (4) Siegel's bound ρ ≤ θ for Pisot numbers of degree at most three (Siegel 1944, restricted; not new; proved through the minimal Mahler measures of registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); (5) under the Padovan rule the word ca is a factor of the fifth iterate from the seed a, and ac is a factor of no iterate from any seed; under its mirror, the reverse. The uniqueness was stated without proof by Mercat (2020) for substitutions on three letters; the contribution is a kernel-checked proof of the combined statement, for every real eigenvalue and with no primitivity, unit or non-erasing hypothesis (in the equality case these are consequences: θ = ρ forces k = 3 and characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1), together with the chirality of both minimal rules. No first-formalization claim is made. That ρ itself is a Pisot eigenvalue of the Padovan matrix, so that the bound is attained, is proved in Supplement.lean and not compared. Companion of registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006.

records.title: The radian nine-gon is Euclidean Ramsey iff e^(i theta) is algebraic
records.abstract: Theorem D: for real theta, the nine points (cos k theta, sin k theta), k = 0, ..., 8, of the Euclidean plane are distinct, lie on the unit circle and are not Euclidean Ramsey when tan(theta/2) is transcendental; and whenever they are distinct, they are Ramsey if and only if cos theta and sin theta are algebraic (that is, iff e^(i theta) is algebraic), if and only if tan(theta/2) is algebraic. This is an iff for a whole one-parameter family, where earlier explicit examples with a transcendental parameter (OpenAI's Proposition 7.7 and Corollary 7.5) settle single sets: the same nine-point pattern is Ramsey or not exactly as e^(i theta) is algebraic or transcendental. Nine is the exact threshold (eight consecutive multiples are Ramsey for every theta; by hand, in spherical-ramsey), and at theta = e the question becomes whether e^(i e) is algebraic, which appears to be open. Ramsey is OpenAI's definition from result 172 (for every r >= 2 there is D such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy). The statements are given in OpenAI's vocabulary plus the two-line definition of the nine points, and again with no definitions beyond Mathlib. The non-Ramsey direction mirrors OpenAI's nine-point proof (their Proposition 7.6): the coordinate field is Q(tan(theta/2)), its tensor square embeds in Q(T, U), and the denominator-cleared 9x9 evaluation matrix is nonsingular, certified at (T, U) = (2, 3) by an explicit integer triangular factorization checked by decide +kernel; OpenAI's linear obstruction concludes. The converse uses the theorem that finite spherical sets with algebraic coordinates are Ramsey (prior work of JD-Jones-ASES, Rogerhu12 and atimics; proved again here in Lean on OpenAI's development). The proof builds on OpenAI's complete Lean proof of the classification (openai/math fd4aeeb2), whose 35 files used here are included with header-only changes for the Lean module system. This repository is a module-system port, with no statement or proof line changed apart from a namespace rename, of Lean already public as rope AV3 of spherical-ramsey v1.1.0 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23396387), packaged so that Theorem D can be checked on its own. All theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.

records.title: Graham's bounds for list scheduling and LPT on identical machines: 2 − 1/m, 4/3 − 1/(3m) and their tight instances
records.abstract: A Lean 4 development of Graham's two bounds for scheduling independent jobs on identical machines to minimize the makespan (R. L. Graham, Bounds for certain multiprocessing anomalies, Bell System Tech. J. 45 (1966) 1563-1581; Bounds on multiprocessing timing anomalies, SIAM J. Appl. Math. 17 (1969) 416-429; both restated with their examples in his survey Bounds on multiprocessing anomalies and related packing algorithms, AFIPS Spring Joint Computer Conference (1972) 205-217). n jobs of nonnegative real lengths p : Fin n -> R are run without interruption on m >= 1 identical machines; an assignment sigma : Fin n -> Fin m loads machine i with the sum of the lengths assigned to it, its makespan is the largest load, and optMakespan m p is the least makespan over all m^n assignments. A list schedule (IsListSchedule, in the index order) gives each job a machine whose load from the earlier jobs is least, under any tie-breaking (a relation, so every theorem covers every tie-breaking); an LPT schedule (IsLPTSchedule) is a list schedule of the jobs in some nonincreasing order of length. Theorems, kernel-only: every list schedule sigma and every assignment tau satisfy m * C(sigma) <= (2m - 1) * C(tau) (Graham 1966, his Theorem for the same number of processors and no precedence constraints), so C(sigma) <= (2 - 1/m) * optMakespan; the m(m - 1) unit jobs followed by one job of length m (Graham's example for his theorem on scheduling the k largest tasks optimally first, at k = 0, as his 1972 survey restates it; Lenstra-Shmoys, Chapter 9, p. 188) have optimum m and every list schedule of them in that order has makespan 2m - 1, so 2 - 1/m is the least constant (IsLeast); every LPT schedule sigma and every assignment tau satisfy 3m * C(sigma) <= (4m - 1) * C(tau) (Graham 1969, Theorem 2, announced in the closing remarks of the 1966 paper), so C(sigma) <= (4/3 - 1/(3m)) * optMakespan; when every job is longer than a third of C(tau), every LPT schedule is at least as good as tau, so LPT is optimal when every job exceeds a third of the optimum; Graham's 2m + 1 jobs 2m - 1, 2m - 1, 2m - 2, 2m - 2, ..., m + 1, m + 1, m, m, m (his pp. 425-426) are in nonincreasing order, have optimum 3m, attained by a list schedule in the order 2m - 1, ..., m + 1, m, m, 2m - 1, ..., m + 1, m (the definition grahamOrder, a permutation of the jobs whose lengths are that list), and every LPT schedule of them has makespan 4m - 1, for every m >= 1, so 4/3 - 1/(3m) is the least constant (IsLeast); and the elementary facts (list and LPT schedules exist, the optimum is attained, every load, every job and the average load are at most the makespan, relabeling the jobs preserves the makespan); Graham's omega_0, the least finishing time over all lists, equals the optimum over all assignments (every assignment is matched or improved by a list schedule in some order), so the bounds against every assignment are his; for his instance the optimum is attained by an explicit list (grahamOrder); and the third of the optimality theorem cannot be weakened (on three machines 9, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, each job at least a third of the optimum 12, has an LPT schedule of makespan 13, so n <= 2m jobs do not make LPT optimal; Graham's 1972 survey prints Spencer's 6, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2 for the same purpose); and the position of a job on its machine: the (c + 1)-th job k placed on a machine of a list schedule of a nonincreasing p has (c + 1) p_k <= C(tau) for every assignment tau (the property of Chen 1993, as Della Croce-Scatamacchia 2020 restate it; proved here by an invariant on pairs of machines), hence the Coffman-Sethi form q m C(sigma) <= ((q + 1) m - 1) C(tau) for a machine with q jobs attaining the makespan of an LPT schedule (Coffman-Sethi 1976 as corrected by Chen 1993, as Della Croce-Scatamacchia restate it; the literature states it for q >= 3, for m >= 2 it is weaker than the 4/3 - 1/(3m) bound at q <= 2, and neither its attainment nor Chen's 4/3 - 1/(3(m - 1)) at q = 2 is proved here; Chen's and Coffman-Sethi's papers were not read). The proof of the LPT bound is by counting, not by his exchange argument: with k the job ending a heaviest machine, the average-load bound settles 3 p_k <= C(tau), and otherwise a count of the jobs up to k (every machine of tau holds at most two of them, those at least as long as the least load sit alone, each single-job machine of sigma contributes one) shows that k's machine ends by C(tau). Further: for a job k completing at the makespan of a list schedule of a nonincreasing p, the smaller of C(sigma) and 3 p_k is at most C(tau) for every tau, and C(sigma) <= 3 p_k certifies optimality; equality 3m C(sigma) = (4m - 1) C(tau) on m >= 2 machines forces 3 p_k = C(tau), equal loads before k, every load of tau equal to C(tau) and no positive job after k; Della Croce-Scatamacchia's Proposition 4, q (m - 1) C(sigma) <= ((q + 1)(m - 1) - 1) C(tau) when another machine holds q jobs before k and q + 2 <= m, proved from Chen's property; Dósa's theorem (2004, Theorem 2: Graham's example is the only tight one): every positive multiple of Graham's 2m + 1 jobs in any order attains the bound, and for a nonempty positive instance on m >= 2 machines a list schedule in nonincreasing order, or an LPT schedule in any order, attains 3m C(sigma) = (4m - 1) optMakespan only when the instance is a positive multiple of Graham's jobs, so the inequality is strict for every number of jobs other than 2m + 1; and for every fixed n >= 2m + 1 the constant 4/3 - 1/(3m) is the supremum (IsLUB) of C(sigma)/optMakespan over the LPT schedules of the positive instances with n jobs (the proof approaches it with Graham's jobs followed by small jobs; Dósa's Remark 1 asserts a strict gap for every n != 2m + 1, which can therefore hold at most for n < 2m + 1, not formalized here). Forty-one compared statements over nine fully specified definitions; the finite facts behind every statement are replayed exactly in the standard library by scripts/check_lpt.py. As of 2026-10-11 no kernel-checked proof of the 4/3 - 1/(3m) bound, of either equality family or of the optimality statement was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, anthropics/formal-math, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index, GitHub code search in Lean or arXiv; the AFP's Approximation_Algorithms proves a 3/2 bound for sorted greedy and the factor 2 for greedy, and two Lean repositories prove m * C <= sum p + (m - 1) * p_max over lists of naturals. No priority is claimed.

records.title: Robbins' theorem on strongly connected orientations
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Robbins' theorem: a finite connected simple graph has a strongly connected orientation (a digraph with underlying graph G, never containing both u → v and v → u, in which every vertex reaches every other) if and only if no edge of it is a bridge. As a corollary, every finite 2-edge-connected graph on a nonempty vertex type has a strongly connected orientation. Mathlib has bridges, edge connectivity and digraphs, but not this theorem.

records.title: Normalizers of Γ_Δ(N): the group M_Δ, finiteness, and a coset count
records.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, about the normalizers in SL₂(ℝ) of the groups Γ_Δ(N) between Γ₁(N) and Γ₀(N), and the quotients Nor(Γ_Δ(N))/Γ_Δ(N), which for −1 ∈ Δ are the modular automorphism groups of the curves X_Δ(N): the matrices allowed by the generalized Newman bound h_Δ form a group M_Δ = D⁻¹Γ₀(n_Δ)⁺D, D = diag(h_Δ, 1), which contains Nor(Γ_Δ(N)) and contains Γ₀(N) with finite index, so Nor(Γ_Δ(N))/Γ_Δ(N) is finite for every Δ; its order is [(ℤ/N)ˣ : Δ] times the number of pairs (σ, H), with σ in a fixed set of representatives of Γ₀(N)\SL₂(ℤ) and H a Hermite normal form, such that σH normalizes Γ_Δ(N); and h_Δ = h(N) except under three explicit conditions on N and Δ. 11 theorems, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Lossy Distance-Shell Tomography on Paths: Recovery from Mean and Covariance
records.abstract: A substantive Lean development of two-leg identifiability under independent relay deletion and nearest-surviving-ancestor bypass. An interior path sensor observes anonymous counts at each contracted hop, superimposing both legs. For every known real survival probability strictly between zero and one, the mean and covariance identify the unordered pair of natural-valued leg populations. A sparse interface needs only the covariance diagonal and one adaptively selected column. The concrete law is a finite sum over independent Bernoulli relay masks. Ten selected statements additionally establish mean/fold equivalence, endpoint trace and degenerate-probability semantics, actual-model variance bounds, conditional integer reconstruction recurrences, and a logarithmic randomized-testing lower bound for actual paths of every length at least two. The full finite-sample probability guarantee is not claimed.

records.title: GromovMilman
records.abstract: Formalization of Theorem 1 (the Gromov–Milman conjecture on polynomials restricted to subspaces) from Dol'nikov–Karasev, "Dvoretzky type theorems for multivariate polynomials and sections of convex bodies" (arXiv:1009.0392): for any even d > 0 and any k, there exists n(d, k) such that every homogeneous polynomial of degree d on R^n (n >= n(d, k)) restricts on some k-dimensional subspace V to a scalar multiple of (x_1^2 + ... + x_n^2)^(d/2). The formalization provides an unconditional, constructive proof without sorry or external topological black boxes: Carlsson's theorem on non-abelian 2-groups is eliminated in favor of an elementary abelian Dold-type Borsuk–Ulam theorem ((Z/2)^r) proved from scratch on chain complexes and applied inductively level-by-level to iterated wreath products via block-structured join embeddings.

records.title: Pointwise a.e. convergence of ergodic averages with respect to two commuting transformations in Lean
records.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the pointwise a.e. convergence theorem for ergodic averages with respect to two commuting transformations. This theorem was proved by GPT 6 Pro when it was instructed to adapt the recent breakthrough on the triangular Hilbert transform made public by OpenAI. The formalization was generated by Claude Opus 5.5 Medium.

records.title: Paracompact expansion and collectionwise separation
records.abstract: Every locally finite indexed family of arbitrary subsets of a paracompact topological space admits a locally finite open expansion with the same index type, without separation assumptions. In a paracompact normal space, a discrete closed family admits a discrete locally finite open expansion whose closures are pairwise disjoint and lie in prescribed open neighborhoods. Consequently every paracompact Hausdorff space is collectionwise normal. Index and ambient types may be empty and have independent universes; the family has unrestricted cardinality. These are classical results; no novelty is claimed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Systolic growth in every genus
records.abstract: This repository introduces and formally proves the lower bound 4/3 for the limit inferior of the supremal hyperbolic systole in genus g divided by log g. At present, this formalization is the theorem's only public statement and proof. This metadata records the result as an original proof; the published papers below are cited only as background for ingredients. The proof combines arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces, uniform representations by comparable prime cubes, and surface gluing followed by a smooth conformal change to curvature minus one that preserves the systole lower bound.

records.title: Galvin's theorem, the Dinitz problem and stable matchings
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Galvin's theorem that the list chromatic index of a finite bipartite graph equals its maximum degree (if every edge has a list of at least Δ colours, a proper edge colouring can be chosen from the lists), of its corollary solving the Dinitz problem (an n × n array with lists of n symbols per cell admits a choice with distinct symbols in every row and column), and of the Gale–Shapley theorem on the existence of stable matchings with strict preferences and incomplete acceptability lists, which provides the kernels in Galvin's argument. Mathlib has line graphs and colourings but none of these results.

records.title: Persistent failure of Euclidean quartic SOS exactness
records.abstract: An explicit rational homogeneous cubic with 25 monomials in 14 real variables has maximum one on the Euclidean unit sphere and admits a positive degree-four moment functional with value 500753357629/500000000000. For every positive real regularization parameter, quadratic strength and cubic strength, the associated quartic has an explicitly attained global minimum whose shift is not a sum of squares of real polynomials. A quantitative strict separation bounds every SOS lower bound. The polynomial is stationary at zero with negative definite Hessian. A second explicit 25-term cubic, certified by the same rational functional, gives a unique global minimizer with positive-definite Hessian there and persistent SOS failure for all positive parameters. The exact sphere maximizers are classified. The proof combines an elementary quadratic-map contraction, a rational moment certificate, an ordinary SOS degree bound and an all-parameter radial factorization.

records.title: Hamiltonian s–t paths in solid grid graphs are decidable in polynomial time
records.abstract: A computable algorithm, decideHamPath, that decides whether a solid grid graph (a finite set of lattice points with no holes, with an edge between points at distance 1) has a Hamiltonian path between two given distinct points, with a Lean 4 proof that it is correct. The problem was posed by Itai, Papadimitriou and Szwarcfiter (1982). The algorithm extends Sheffield's height-function algorithm for Hamiltonian cycles: each endpoint gets a phantom edge to a missing neighbour, and an endpoint with all eight neighbours present becomes a hole whose defect (a vortex) is handled by a slit height and a search over flip classes. The registered statement is correctness. The library also proves a polynomial step bound, 5 220 000 (|V| + 3)^6, for cost functions written beside the algorithm, and formalizes the Umans–Lenhart algorithm for Hamiltonian cycles in solid grid graphs.

records.title: A Unified Kalman-Type Classification of Controllability for Linear Stochastic Systems
records.abstract: Formalization of a finite algebraic classification of approximate, approximate null, exact null, and exact controllability for finite-dimensional linear stochastic systems with constant coefficients and independent Brownian drivers. A decreasing subspace sequence gives a common obstruction for the first three properties; exact controllability additionally requires full row rank of the stacked diffusion-control matrix. The development also covers stochastic integration, forward and backward equations, duality, finite rank tests, null feedback, and polynomial small-time energy bounds. The independent Palomar statement and its solution compile with Lean v4.35.0-rc2 and canonical Mathlib. Complete sandboxed mechanical preflight and editorial review are separate requirements; no registration is claimed.

records.title: Survival and transience above the compartment-division threshold
records.abstract: Survival and transience are established throughout the strictly supercritical regime of the noncoagulating compartment model of Anderson, Howells and Rojas La Luz (https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10223v4, Remark 4.8). Compartments produce molecules at rate b, degrade them at rate d per molecule, exit at rate e, and divide at rate f per molecule, with arbitrary conservative allocation between the daughters. For b,e,f > 0 and d >= 0 with bf > e(e+d), every finite nonempty family has positive probability of eternal survival, with an explicit product lower bound. For positive immigration intensity and any distribution of finite immigrant contents, the process is nonexplosive and the expected total physical occupation time of every compartment-count state has an explicit finite bound. This establishes the transience conjectured in Remark 4.8 without a moment assumption on immigrant contents. The quantitative bounds use a positive eigenweight of the mean system and a bounded multiplicative barrier; a distribution-dependent immigration constant sharpens the uniform occupation bound.

records.title: Omega-bounded Sigma-products and a sharp compactness criterion
records.abstract: For arbitrary T1 omega-bounded factors with an explicit product basepoint, the countable-support Sigma-product is omega-bounded and countably compact. Every countable family is trapped, together with its ambient closure, in a closed compact coordinate box using one countable support. For compact Hausdorff factors, the Sigma-product is compact if and only if only countably many factors contain a point different from the basepoint. Uncountable discrete Boolean Sigma-products are countably compact but not compact. The index and factor universes are independent; the empty index and empty countable subsets are allowed. No first-countability or separability premise is added.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Exact db2 cascade norms and an optimal uniform constant
records.abstract: Exact supremum-operator norms for the undecimated periodic db2 cascade. For every level j and every period N at least the support, the norm is c_j^d, where c_j = 1651/1395 - (4/63)4^{-j} + (1/180)16^{-j} - (1/1736)32^{-j}. For every positive period, aliasing included, the norm is at most (1651/1395)^d, and that power is the least constant with this uniform role. The free mass is strictly increasing, converges to 1651/1395, and the gap is at most (4/63)4^{-j}. Dimension zero is exactly 1. N at least the support is sufficient, not claimed necessary, and one fixed period is not claimed to attain the limit. At dimension zero the least-constant conclusion is 1 ≤ B; it does not force B = 1. The level-one kernel is the seven-tap half-autocorrelation, with norm (9/8)^d for N >= 7. Levels 1, 2 and 3 remain the exact values (299/256)^d, (9663/8192)^d and (309991/262144)^d for N >= 19, 43 and 91. Bibliographic priority of the closed form is unresolved; see docs/RELATED_WORK.md. A conditional propagation then carries a supplied summary Lipschitz bound and a supplied seminorm comparison through the level-one operator. Bottleneck stability, persistence diagrams and landscape non-expansiveness are hypotheses, not theorems. Those conditional statements are retained in the sources as auxiliaries and are not selected. Nineteen statements are selected. They are parts of this development, not nineteen independent contributions. The exposition of the cascade argument is docs/CASCADE_THEOREM.md.

records.title: Countable cellularity of arbitrary products via finite subproducts
records.abstract: An arbitrary product of topological spaces satisfies the countable chain condition (CCC) whenever every finite subproduct does. For nonempty factors this is an equivalence. The proof includes an indexed uncountable delta-system lemma that permits repeated finite supports, and glues compatible cylinders over a finite common root. Arbitrary products of separable spaces are consequently CCC, without a cardinal bound or separation assumptions and allowing empty factors. Continuous-surjection preservation and the discrete-space countability criterion are proved companions. No unrestricted productivity of CCC factors or productively-CCC theorem is asserted.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: Erdős Problem 111: bipartizing finite subgraphs of uncountably chromatic graphs
records.abstract: A Lean proof that for every real C, a graph whose finite subgraphs on m vertices can each be made bipartite by deleting at most Cm edges has countable chromatic number. Hence h_G(n)/n → ∞ for every graph G that is not countably colorable, in particular for every graph of chromatic number ℵ₁. This answers the second question of Erdős Problem 111 in the affirmative.

records.title: Erdős Problem 173: monochromatic triangles in two-colorings of the plane
records.abstract: A Lean proof that in every two-coloring of the plane any three distinct points that are not the vertices of an equilateral triangle, collinear points included, have a monochromatic congruent copy and at most one equilateral side length is missed, so at most one triangle up to congruence, degenerate or not, has no monochromatic copy. Alternating strips show that one equilateral triangle can be missed. This answers Erdős Problem 173 as Bloom states it and settles the conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer and Straus that every non-equilateral triangle has a monochromatic copy, collinear triples included; it is new to our knowledge. The step from arbitrary to measurable colorings adapts OpenAI's rigidity theorem for wild character laws, extended here from the algebraic numbers to the algebraic closure of ℚ(x) in ℂ for every real x, and its transfer from proper to weak measurable colorings.

records.title: Erdős Problem 408: distribution of iterated totient heights
records.abstract: A Lean proof that the least k with φ_k(n) = 1 has normal order α log n for a constant 1 / log 3 ≤ α ≤ 1 / log 2, with mean-square error O(x (log x)² / (log log x)⁵). This answers the first two questions of Erdős Problem 408. The proof formalizes extensions of Theorems 3.1 and 6.1 of OpenAI's The Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors, and uses vendored Lean proofs of the zero-free half-plane re s > 7/8 for Dirichlet L-functions (openai/math) and of the weighted dilation graph results (Yao Xu's totient-fibers-lean4).

records.title: Exact fault images in priority controllers
records.abstract: Exact reachable qualifier-set images for a finite priority controller with independent enable and request inputs and a specified first-stage bridge interface. The formal statements characterize detection through arbitrary Boolean qualifier observations, show that nonemptiness cannot be expressed by valid proper-coordinate relations, and classify a specified qualifier-only stuck-at fault. The selector and fault equations are explicit.

records.title: Falconer's distance problem for stretched logarithmic gauges
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.1 of the supplied October 2026 manuscript: every compact subset of the Euclidean plane with positive Hausdorff measure for the gauge r exp(-(log(1/r))^theta), with 2/3 < theta < 1, has a distance set of positive Lebesgue measure. The proof constructs gauge Frostman probabilities with finite logarithmic critical and Fourier energies, obtains the required radial Orlicz densities, and decomposes the measures into finite-depth regular pieces. Measurable directional tests and smooth masks define actual filtered distance measures with summable removed mass. Quantitative stationary phase, inverse operators, orthogonality, distance linearization, and space splitting prove all four induction recurrences for the actual energies. A weighted finite-tree argument yields summable frequency-shell bounds; Fourier reconstruction gives absolute continuity of a nonzero weighted distance measure and hence the stated positive Lebesgue measure. The target theorem builds without proof holes and uses only the three standard Lean axioms. Source adaptations are recorded under fidelity.

records.title: Kuhn poker: the value −1/18, all optimal strategies, and the solution at every ante and bet
records.abstract: A Lean 4 development of Kuhn's simplified two-person poker (Kuhn 1950): three cards 1 < 2 < 3, one dealt to each player with the six deals equiprobable, an ante of a from each player and a single bet of b, player I acting first, the five courses of play of Kuhn's p. 98 with payoffs a (pass-pass, to the higher card), a to II (pass-bet-pass), a + b to the higher card (pass-bet-bet), a to I (bet-pass) and a + b to the higher card (bet-bet). The definitions are built from the game tree: a behaviour strategy of I is a pair of functions on the three cards (the probability of betting first, the probability of calling after passing and facing a bet), one of II likewise (the probability of betting after a pass, the probability of calling a bet); the payoff is the average over the six deals; a strategy guarantees v when it is valid and earns at least v (holds the opponent to at most v) against every valid strategy of the opponent; the game has value v when each player has a strategy guaranteeing v; an equilibrium is a saddle point. For Kuhn's game a = b = 1, kernel-checked: the value is -1/18 (a game has at most one value), an equilibrium exists, every equilibrium pays I exactly -1/18, and a pair is an equilibrium iff each strategy guarantees -1/18; II's optimal strategy is unique at all six information sets (bet after a pass with the 1, 2, 3 with probabilities 1/3, 0, 1; call with probabilities 0, 1/3, 1 - Kuhn's (xi, eta) = (1/3, 1/3) with the four coordinates he removed as superfluous now proved forced); I's optimal strategies are exactly Kuhn's one-parameter family (bet the 1 with probability alpha and fold it, never bet the 2 first and call with it with probability alpha + 1/3, bet the 3 with probability 3 alpha and call with it, for alpha in [0, 1/3], the call with the 3 being unconstrained exactly when 3 alpha = 1, where that information set is unreached); in the normal form with Kuhn's coding of the 27 and 64 pure strategies, his essential 8 x 4 matrix is six times the game matrix, his twelve basic optimal mixed strategies (A)-(L) and II's two guarantee -1/18, and a mixed strategy is optimal iff its realization plan lies on the family (I) or its marginals are II's strategy (II). For every ante a > 0 and bet b > 0 (Kuhn's pp. 102-103, stated there without proof, and the region b > 2a he does not state): the value is -b^2/(6(2a + b)) for b <= a, -b(2a - b)/(6(2a + b)) for a <= b <= 2a and 0 for b >= 2a, with explicit guaranteeing strategies in each case; in Case 3 the calling probability eta with the 2 ranges over [(2a - b)/(2a + b), b/(2a + b)], and the interval printed on p. 102, b/(2a + b) <= eta <= (a + b)/(2a + b), fails at its upper end (at a = 2, b = 3 and eta = 5/7 II's Case 3 strategy does not guarantee the value). Every guarantee is a finite nonnegative-product identity (the gap between the payoff and the value is a sum of products of the opponent's probabilities and their complements with coefficients nonnegative on the case's region: polynomials in a, b and the free parameter, at general stakes built from a, b, 2a + b, a - b, 2a - b, 4a - b, b - 2a and the interval factors (2a + b)eta - (2a - b), b - (2a + b)eta, 2(a - b) - (2a + b)xi, and, in the optimal-set theorems, the slacks of their stated inequalities), and every "only if" is a linear certificate from finitely many pure strategies (the coefficients rationals at a = b = 1 and, at general stakes, polynomials in a, b and the free parameter nonnegative on the case's region); no formal library found by the dated search holds the game. Beyond Kuhn's statements: the two certificate identities are stated as theorems; the equilibria of Kuhn's game are exactly the pairs (kuhnI α k, kuhnII) with α in [0, 1/3], k in [0, 1] and 3α = 1 or k = 1; and at general stakes the optimal sets are determined - I's strategy is unique for b < a (up to the unreached call with the 3) and for a < b <= 2a, is Kuhn's family on the diagonal b = a at every scale, and for b >= 2a never bets the 1 or the 2 first, folds them, and with the 3 is cut out by one inequality (a single strategy at b = 2a; beyond it a two-dimensional set in which I may also bet the 3 first, with probability at most (b - 2a)/b), so Kuhn's one-parameter family is optimal only at b = a; II's strategy is unique on the diagonal at every scale and a segment for b <= a (the bet with the 2 after a pass free in [0, 2(a - b)/(2a + b)], so Kuhn's 'unique optimal mode of behavior' in Case 1 holds in his behaviour parameters only); for a <= b < 2a its bets after a pass are forced, (b/(2a + b), 0, 1), and its calls form a polytope of three inequalities; for b > 2a it never bets the 1 or the 2 after a pass, never calls with them, and calls with the 3 with probability at least 4a/(2a + b), its bet with the 3 free; and on the line b = 2a its optimal set is a five-dimensional polytope (the bet with the 2 after a pass zero and, with bets (p, 0, r) and calls (s, t, w), 2p <= r, s + t <= p, 1 <= t + w, 1 + p + s <= 2w; nine vertices, replayed); at every ante a > 0 and bet b > 0 every equilibrium pays the value and a pair is an equilibrium iff each strategy guarantees it, so the equilibria are exactly the pairs of optimal strategies, on b = 2a explicitly; the corrected Case 3 interval is sharp, and the printed one holds only at its lower end. A second correction, a misprint, is noted in the documentation: p. 101's table gives β = 5/12 for (I) and (J), where p. 100's mixtures and p. 101's own formula give 7/12.

records.title: The Alon–Tarsi theorem and 3-choosability of planar bipartite graphs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Alon–Tarsi theorem: if a finite simple graph has an orientation whose numbers of even and odd Eulerian subdigraphs differ, then it can be properly coloured from any lists larger than the out-degrees; and of its corollary that every finite planar bipartite graph is 3-choosable. Planarity is the combinatorial notion of a plane map (a rotation system of genus zero) of the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-15-000005, whose definitions are reproduced verbatim in the Challenge. The proof uses the graph polynomial and Mathlib's Combinatorial Nullstellensatz, Euler's formula for plane maps, and an out-degree-2 orientation obtained from Hall's theorem.

records.title: Guarded detection and constrained eligible-set extensions
records.abstract: Correctness and completeness of fault detection and extension over a supplied guarded decoder DAG, together with an executed native cold-detector bound.

records.title: Barker sequences of odd length have length 1, 3, 5, 7, 11 or 13
records.abstract: A Lean 4 development of the classification of Barker sequences of odd length. A Barker sequence of length n is a sequence h of n signs whose aperiodic autocorrelations C(k), the sum over j < n - k of h(j) h(j + k), satisfy |C(k)| <= 1 for 0 < k < n. Turyn and Storer (1961) stated, and gave a proof, that a Barker sequence of odd length n > 1 has length 3, 5, 7, 11 or 13 (length 1 is admitted here: it has no nontrivial shift). Theorem 1(iv) of Turyn–Storer, on which their proof relies, is false as stated (Willms 2014, explicit counterexamples); per Schmidt–Willms (footnote 1) parts (ii) and (iii) imply (iv) on a corrected range that suffices for the induction, and independent proofs exist (Borwein–Erdélyi 2013; Schmidt–Willms 2016, the proof formalized here). The proof formalized is that of Schmidt and Willms (2016), recast so that the classification needs no enumeration of sequences: for odd n and m = (n - 1)/2, odd shifts have autocorrelation 0 and even shifts (-1)^m (from C(u) + C(n - u) = n mod 4); skew-symmetry h(k) h(n - 1 - k) = (-1)^(m + k); the folded identity, the sum over k <= w of (-1)^k h(k) h(w - k), equals 1 for every even w <= n - 3; the doubling law h(u - 1) h(u) = h(2u - 1) h(2u) for 1 <= u <= (n - 3)/2; Schmidt and Willms's Lemmas 3 and 4 in sign-change form (for n >= 7 and h(0) = h(1), with p the first sign change and q the first sign change not divisible by p, both are odd and 2q - 3 <= n <= p + q + 1, Lemma 4 by one generating-function identity for the folded sums); and an endgame that leaves n in {7, 11, 13}, excluding n = 9 by skew-symmetry and doubling, with the alternation h(j) -> (-1)^j h(j) for the normalization h(0) = h(1). Eight witnesses, one at each length 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11 and 13, are Barker by decide, and every Barker sequence of odd length equals a fixed sequence of its length (canon) up to negation and alternation, by a kernel enumeration of the 2^n sign patterns at each of the six odd lengths. Also proved: the even reduction of Turyn and Storer's footnote 2, that a Barker sequence of even length n > 2 has 4 | n and yields a real circulant Hadamard matrix of order n. Given the even-length classification as an explicit hypothesis (every Barker sequence of positive even length has length 2 or 4, the statement even_length_eq_two_or_four of openai/math, family 179), a Barker sequence of positive length n exists exactly when n is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11 or 13, and every Barker sequence has length at most 13; the same follows from the hypothesis that real circulant Hadamard matrices of positive order exist only at orders 1 and 4 (the forward direction of exists_iff_order_one_or_four of openai/math), through the even reduction. The seven definitions are restated from openai/math's two challenge files, character for character except the two Fin-bound proofs inside aperiodic (explicit terms in place of by omega, which under the module system yields module-private auxiliary theorems the comparator rejects), so its two theorems discharge the hypotheses, even_length_eq_two_or_four by unfolding alone and exists_iff_order_one_or_four by unfolding and Iff.mp; they are not proved here. The restated definitions and the adapted parts named in NOTICE derive from Apache-2.0 work of OpenAI (NOTICE, LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt); the rest is MIT.

records.title: Canonical streaming enumeration of eligible detections
